I have fixed the infinite loop in `Text.append` by creating a shallow copy of `self._spans` before iterating over it. This prevents the loop when a `Text` object is appended to itself. I verified the fix with a reproduction script and a test case.

The infinite loop in the `append` method of the `Text` class in the `rich` library was caused by iterating over `self._spans` while simultaneously extending it when a `Text` object was appended to itself (`t.append(t)`). This occurred because the generator expression used in `self._spans.extend()` continued to find new elements as they were added to the list.

I fixed this by wrapping `text._spans` in a `list()` call, which creates a shallow copy (snapshot) of the spans before iteration begins. This ensures that the iteration is performed over the original set of spans, preventing the infinite loop.

- Modified `rich/text.py`: In the `append` method, changed the iteration over `text._spans` to iterate over `list(text._spans)`.
